clue.text: Auditorium bag, not old

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to leave the following word out of the bag word

parts.note: a holdall is a large travelling bag
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone describing a concert hall's bag, perhaps a lost-property item that is new.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove OLD from HOLDALL and HALL is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall is a large room or building for concerts and lectures, the same thing as an auditorium.

clue.text: Old vehicles from church, with a bold, colourful display on Sabbath

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
the article taken as written
a riot of colour is a vivid, bold display
S is an abbreviation for Sabbath, placed last

explanation.surface: Antique carriages turn out from church in a bright parade on Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariots were the two-wheeled horse-drawn carts of ancient warfare and racing, plainly vehicles of old.

clue.text: Dramatist put away? No way!

indicators.note: 'No way!' read literally orders the word for a way to be dropped

parts.note: to put away food is to eat or ingest it
ST, street, is a way; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Was the playwright locked up? Surely not!
explanation.walkthrough: William Inge was an American playwright (Picnic, Bus Stop). Take ST from INGEST.
explanation.definitionFit: William Inge wrote plays for Broadway in the 1950s, so he is a dramatist.

clue.text: IT broadcast with Naples' most outspoken

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so these letters are flung into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the city name taken as written

explanation.surface: Information technology aired alongside a Neapolitan programme is the bluntest of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain speech is frank and direct, so the plainest speaker is the most outspoken.

clue.text: Horse you could tell the time by?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse bred and ridden for fox-hunting

definitions.text: you could tell the time by
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pocket watch with a hinged metal cover over the face

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke of a horse that tells the time; the second meaning is a full-hunter pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sturdy riding horse used in the hunting field and a lidded pocket watch, an item you read the time from.

clue.text: Youngster going round ship getting kicks — overbearing type

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece is wrapped about another

parts.note: a boy is a youngster
SS, steamship, prefixes ship names
to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: A lad circling a vessel and lashing out with his feet is behaving like a domineering tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' looks like thrills, but it is the verb for striking with a foot; the ship goes inside the youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossyboots is an informal British label for someone who keeps ordering others about.

clue.text: Needing specs to see one's old photograph

parts.note: my is what one says of what is one's own
O is a standard abbreviation for old
pic is short for picture or photograph

explanation.surface: Someone needs glasses to look at an old snapshot of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sighted person cannot see distant things clearly without spectacles, which is what myopia means.

clue.text: Stag do evening eventually starts with Rex

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A stag party night ends, at last, with someone called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag do' looks like a bachelor party; 'Stag' alone is the definition and 'do' starts the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, so the animal is named by its male example.

clue.text: White female featured in article

indicators.note: something featured in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A pale woman appears in a magazine story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece in a magazine, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face gone pale grey with shock, a synonym for white in that sense.

clue.text: Blood cell cycle out — rebooted with drug

indicators.note: rebooting restarts a system afresh, so these letters are set up again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A computer instruction: end the blood-cell cycle and restart the system with a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A leucocyte is a white blood cell, the body's infection fighter, so it is one kind of blood cell.

clue.text: Lawbreaker demanding tip to store working crane

indicators.note: something working is in operation, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement
to store something is to hold it inside, so one piece keeps another within

parts.note: to tip and to list both mean to lean over
the word crane rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal insists that a builder's crane be kept at the rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a rubbish dump, but here it means lean, LIST; the shuffled crane goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, the crime of theft, so is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Policeman's drink on retirement

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the small word before it is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning; it is turned round

explanation.surface: A police officer's tipple after leaving the force.
explanation.walkthrough: SUP, then RE read backwards as ER. A super is short for a superintendent, a senior British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is the informal short form of superintendent, a senior officer rank in British police forces.

clue.text: Northerner — I say! — bagging Dior creation

indicators.note: a fashion creation is something made up, so these letters are made into a new order
bagging something captures it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise, like I say!
the designer's name rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from the north exclaims as he snaps up a Dior design.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled DIOR goes inside GEE. A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geordie comes from Tyneside in north-east England, so is one particular kind of northerner.

clue.text: Top soldier and officer going round Spain

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the officer's letters wrap about the country

parts.note: LT abbreviates lieutenant
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A senior soldier and a fellow officer tour Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top soldier' reads as a commander, but 'Top' is the definition. E for Spain comes from international car plates (España).
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless padded jacket or waistcoat, an upper garment and so a top.

clue.text: Sound as a bell, taking in Saigon excursion, being a doctor?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by example: diagnosing is what a doctor does

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering trip, so the city's letters roam into a new order
taking something in absorbs it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ding is the sound a bell makes
the city name rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic, fit as a fiddle, fits in a trip to Saigon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' suggests perfect health, but it is the noise a bell makes. The rearranged SAIGON goes inside DING.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnosing illness is a core part of a physician's job, so it is a fair example of acting as a doctor.

clue.text: Medieval instrument about to be given a novel name

parts.note: a rebec is a medieval bowed string instrument
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: An old stringed instrument is going to be given an original name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like it means new, but it points to a book title: Daphne du Maurier's Rebecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is a woman's name that also titles Daphne du Maurier's famous novel.

clue.text: Musical sort of basket, open-ended

indicators.note: open-ended means with the ends removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a pannier is a basket slung on a bicycle or a pack animal

explanation.surface: A hamper used in a stage show has its top left open.
explanation.walkthrough: PANNIER without its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the Broadway musical about the orphan Little Orphan Annie, so it is a stage musical.

clue.text: No limits to returning serfs' fever

definitions.note: Lassa names the fever; the answer is the first word of Lassa fever

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from end to start
without limits means without its boundary letters, so first and last are dropped

parts.note: vassals were feudal serfs; read backwards this gives SLASSAV

explanation.surface: Peasants coming home bring a fever with no bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse VASSALS and strip both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic illness named after a town in Nigeria, so Lassa stands for that fever.

clue.text: Singer, Jack, appearing in scholarly books

indicators.note: appearing in something means being inside it, so the name goes within the books

parts.note: tomes are large, weighty books
Jack is a pet form of John, here spelt JON

explanation.surface: A vocalist called Jack features in academic volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' could suggest a bird; it is the Welsh pop star. Jack is a traditional pet form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tom Jones is the Welsh pop vocalist famous for It's Not Unusual and Delilah.

clue.text: Doctor carries one thing around for a certain time

indicators.note: around here means turned about and jumbled, so the word's letters are rearranged
carrying something means holding it, so the doctor's letters enclose the one

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
I is the Roman numeral for one
the word thing rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician carries a single item around for some specific hour.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside MD, then THING is rearranged after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, one exact hour, so it is a particular time.

clue.text: Cold English houses of the past

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the phrase before it holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Chilly English homes belonged to bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective meaning belonging to former times, as in the olden days.

clue.text: Put your foot down (ostentatiously high-heeled?) to take part in this contest

definitions.text: Put your foot down (ostentatiously high-heeled?) to take part in this contest

parts.note: surface reading: to accelerate hard in a car, or to insist firmly
setter's reading: the bracket hints at flamboyant cross-dressing in stilettos, the other sense of the first word of the contest

explanation.walkthrough: The contest is a sprint between cars from a standing start, where the driver floors the pedal; the bracket adds the joke of a race run in drag, wearing showy high heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short acceleration contest between two cars over a straight quarter-mile.

clue.text: Bird caught outside one avian centre, which didn't go down well

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around, so the first pair of pieces surround the next

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
an means one

indicators.note: 'centre' keeps only the middle letter of 'avian'

parts.note: the middle letter of avian
C stands for caught in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A bird nabbed outside, at the heart of some bird sanctuary, was not well received.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT and C go outside AN and I: TIT, AN, I, C. The definition is ironic: the ship certainly went down, but not well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic sank disastrously on its maiden voyage in 1912, an ill-fated going-down, which the clue wryly understates.

clue.text: Flog a church set of Old Testament books

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
taken as written
CH abbreviates church

explanation.surface: An instruction to sell off a church's set of scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' could mean sell, but here it means beat, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanach is the Hebrew Bible, the Jewish canon that Christians call the Old Testament.

clue.text: Bully and lout backing up a dishonest tradesman

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them

indicators.note: backing up in a down answer means moving upward, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout; reversed it reads BOY

explanation.surface: A bully and a thug support a crooked tradesman.
explanation.walkthrough: COW, then YOB read upward. 'Bully' looks like a noun but works as the verb, to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a cowboy is an unqualified or unscrupulous builder or tradesman who does shoddy work.

clue.text: US state has scope to perform a dental operation

parts.note: DE is the postal code for Delaware
scope and scale both mean extent; has joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: An American state has the remit to carry out dentistry.
explanation.definitionFit: To descale teeth is to remove tartar from them, a routine procedure at the dentist or hygienist.

clue.text: See 18
Stick with British post

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast
B abbreviates British

explanation.surface: Persevere with Royal Mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail, but it is an upright of a door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is an upright side piece of a door or window frame, effectively a vertical post.

clue.text: Don't jump the gun — hang on pending the computer experts!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a call to hold back until the right moment

definitions.text: hang on pending the computer experts
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: wait until IT, the information technology staff, arrive

explanation.walkthrough: IT is the usual office name for the computer support department, so the phrase reads literally as waiting for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a drill-sergeant's or comedian's call to hold off acting until the proper moment, and literally means awaiting IT.

clue.text: Passion tree with bifurcate tip

parts.note: a fir is a conifer

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A forked tree top fuels desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire is used figuratively for burning ardour or intense emotion, a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Story about disposing of Roger's trinkets

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
disposing of something gets rid of it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
Roger is the radio code word for R; it is removed

explanation.surface: A tale of Roger throwing out his knick-knacks.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from STORY, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys can mean trifles or baubles of little value, much the same as trinkets.

clue.text: Old PC from celebrated British designer, short of some memory

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the following piece is taken away

parts.note: Charles Rennie Mackintosh, the Glasgow architect and designer
K, a kilobyte, is a small amount of computer memory; removed

explanation.surface: A vintage computer from a famous British designer is low on memory.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K from MACKINTOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple Macintosh, launched in 1984, is an early personal computer.

clue.text: Staggering mythical bird at Killarney's outskirts

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so only the outer letters of the place name are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: A legendary bird reels around the edge of an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' looks like amazing, but it means unsteady on the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means unsteady or wobbly, as of someone tottering, so it fits staggering in that sense.
